abstract:
BackgroundIn vitro expansion of human dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) in serum-free, three-dimensional suspension culture is important for scalable, clinically relevant manufacturing. However, this approach is limited by reduced proliferative capacity and passage-dependent senescence accumulation. In this study, we evaluated whether insulin supplementation could address these limitations while maintaining mesenchymal immunophenotype and stemness-related gene expression across serial passages in a downscale model as a reference for further DPSCs upscaling.

MethodsDPSCs were expanded as spheroids for five consecutive 8-day passages (40 days total) in serum-free medium (SF), serum-free medium supplemented with insulin (SF+I), or medium containing 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS). Spheroid diameter, cell-equivalent yield, and fold expansion per passage were quantified. qPCR analysis of proliferation-associated (Ki67, PCNA), senescence-associated (p16, p21), and stemness-associated (OCT4, SOX2, NANOG, KLF4) transcripts, SA-{beta}-galactosidase staining, and flow-cytometric analysis of MSC-associated surface markers were performed.

ResultsSF+I increased per-passage fold expansion relative to SF and produced expansion values that were comparable from those in FBS (22.3 fold vs 25.0 fold) with larger spheroid diameters. SF showed progressive upregulation of senescence marker p16 and p21 across passages (2.7-fold increase from passage 1 to passage 5), whereas SF+I maintained lower expression of both markers and showed markedly less SA-{beta}-galactosidase positivity at passage 5, compared with SF-based medium (13.19% vs 46.81%). KLF4 and NANOG were better retained in Sf and SF+I under serum-free conditions than under FBS, although the statistical differences were marker-specific. SF and SF+I also retained high positivity for CD105, CD90, and CD73 (>90%), whereas FBS showed substantial loss of these MSC-associated markers (CD90: 31.6%; CD73: 28.4%).

ConclusionsInsulin supplementation supported long-term serum-free 3D DPSC expansion and was associated with lower senescence-associated readouts. Serum-free conditions were also associated with better preservation of the measured MSC-associated surface-marker profile and selected stemness-associated transcripts than FBS conditions. These findings warrant further multi-donor and functional validation of insulin-supplemented serum-free media for DPSC manufacturing.
